first_payload.question: Seven TrueHD titles exited 7 on 'element runs past the payload'. Is the payload cut short, as the project held since 0.4.0?
first_payload.method: 60-second heads. The first payload's last element declares more bytes than the payload holds; truehdd warns 'Truncated oa_element_md' and reads on. Event sequences compared per object, allowing the known +32 sample term.
titles: Pirates of the Caribbean Dead Men Tell No Tales (2017)
first_payload.against_the_old_binary: Pirates head: 3624 events became 3638 before the extended precision fix, every old event unchanged and fourteen added, one per element of the first payload.
first_payload.answer: No. The content is complete and the size is stale. truehdd's warning is the same size check.
first_payload.where: The first access unit, and the access units at seamless branches

fill_after_the_element.reading: On all seven heads every element, these included, ends less than a byte of zero fill before the end of its payload. A payload cut short could not do that.

first_payload.still_refused: An element past the payload whose bits run out, that more than a byte or non-zero fill follows, whose id has no syntax, or with another after it.

whole_tracks.method: The whole track, old and new binary. A verify still at 7 has a fault of its own, named in first_error, which truehdd and FFmpeg were asked about.

whole_tracks.still_at_seven: Coco (2017) and The Incredibles (2004) have faults of their own past the head, in the audio substreams of these copies. truehdd calls both non-conformant with a fatal diagnostic. Their object metadata reads clean.

extended_precision.question: Which reading of ext_prec_pos_presence did the encoder write?
extended_precision.stream: Pirates of the Caribbean Dead Men Tell No Tales (2017), TrueHD, first 60 seconds: the one track in 144 with an extended object element
extended_precision.method: Throwaway builds with the position clamp removed, one per reading, decode --all-events. A refinement of a position stays in the room, and objects move smoothly; neither test asks another decoder.
